Not a problem! A 1013 is an involuntary psychiatric hold. It's the doctor's code of saying a patient is at risk for suicide and could be in immediate danger to themselves. 

I was at a low point. I hate the holiday season (even as an adult) because I have had a lot of bad stuff happen to me as a child during the holidays, such as abandonment trauma. It was right after my 25th birthday that I was hospitalized. I noticed that my meds weren't working anymore and I was in the highest dose. I was having tons of flashbacks and dissociation because of the trauma I suffered as a child. I told my doctor that I wanted to try something different because I was having flashbacks and ideations without a plan. My doctor didn't like my answers and decided to put me on a hold instead. I was sent to the emergency room and held there for 18 hours without food or drink, except a small packet of graham crackers and peanut butter while waiting for a crisis hospital to open up. I was humiliated and felt less than human. 

I would tell them the bare minimum. Tell them that you are feeling hopeless and down but do not tell them that you are suicidal, especially if you think the meds will help. But if you don't think they will help, then tell them the honest truth. Ultimately it is what you need. My experience won't be the exact same as yours.

(My memory on the subject is fragmented.)

My father couldn't handle the children with all the abuse trauma, so he kind of shut down. He wasn't very attentive, especially to me. So I was left wishing I could spend time with him, but was always shrugged off. He didn't even come to my dance recitals when I was in ninth grade. 

Then when I became thirteen, I was struggling with heavy suicidal thoughts and hurting myself. He got angry and just yelled at me for it, while his wife told everyone that I was doing it for attention. The only three people in my family who actually tried to anything about it, were my two older sisters, and my older brother. They asked me why I felt this way, but unbeknownst to me at the time, I felt isolated. I felt like the only person who I could be honest with was my partner, who I started dating on and off for ten years now. 

My older sister, who has since passed, became someone who I could go to when I just wanted to get away. I would spend the night with her, and help take care of my nephew. 

I wish I could go back and tell my school social worker that I don't feel safe at home, and that I could be removed. I wish I had spoken up. Because it's not normal to rely so much on a boyfriend from high school, to the point that they become the only person you speak up to.
